gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of dual-4K loop footage each camera fits on the same card. Working from per-channel bitrates, a 512 GB card holds about 20.3 h on the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K, 17.0 h on the 70mai A900 Ultra and 12.5 h on the VIOFO A229 Ultra 2CH at its maximum bitrate.
standout_why: I compared against productbible.com/blog/best-4k-dash-cams, which ChatGPT cited in chat 2. It divides price by channel count and gives recording time per card only for the Thinkware U3000 PRO (64 GB = 125 min front+rear), the Nextbase 622GW (front only) and the BlackVue Elite 10 1CH (front only). It gives no bitrate and no time per card for any camera recording 4K front and 4K rear. ChatGPT's own answer only says two 4K streams 'consume significant space' and gives no number. I couldn't open caranddriver.com (the fetch tool is blocked there) or thecargearguide.com (certificate error), so I didn't check them; standout is 2 rather than 3 for that reason too.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K belongs in the top three. It is one of four true 4K-front plus 4K-rear cameras I found, and on equal card sizes it keeps the longest loop: about 1.6× the VIOFO A229 Ultra 2CH (20.3 h vs 12.5 h on 512 GB) and about 1.2× the 70mai A900 Ultra (20.3 h vs 17.0 h). The reason is its lower H.265 bitrate (32 + 24 Mbps average). VIOFO's H.264 at 60 + 35 Mbps spends far more data per minute. So the VIOFO can still win on detail per frame, while the Vantrue wins on hours stored per card (and per dollar of card). The 70mai's rear camera drops to 24 fps when both cameras record (rcg530, DashCamTalk), which is a point against it on the question's own terms.
